intro: Distributed workers can summarize partitions without sharing raw records. Merging their centered moments must account for the distance between partition means.
task: Merge worker moment summaries and retain the between-partition contribution that a simple sum of local variances misses.
requirements: counts, means, and m2s are equal-length vectors. Counts are integer-valued in [0,1000000]; m2s are nonnegative sums of centered squared deviations.
Zero-count partitions must have mean=0 and m2=0. Merge all partitions and return dict count, mean, m2; return all zeros when every partition is empty.
When combining states A and B, add m2_A+m2_B+delta^2*n_A*n_B/(n_A+n_B), where delta=mean_B-mean_A. Weight the merged mean by partition counts.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Within-partition variance is insufficient
hints.body: Different partition means contribute additional squared deviations after merging.

hints.title: Treat empty states as identities
hints.body: Skip an empty partition before dividing by the combined count.

explanation: Centered sums are measured around local means. A merged mean moves those centers, producing the between-partition correction in addition to the within-partition m2 totals.
The same sufficient statistics support streaming and distributed aggregation. In exact arithmetic merging is associative; floating-point order can cause small numerical differences.
